Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the action again! Pakistan players are out there in the middle. The opening batters for Bangladesh, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam are there in the middle too. Shaheen Afridi to start with the ball for Pakistan.

So Pakistan now need 10 wickets and have almost a full day in front of them now. The match now looks heavily in the favour of Pakistan and Bangladesh will have to come out with different tactics if they have to survive till the end of the day.

Shaheen Afridi set the tone with a brilliant first over on Day 4. After that, the spinners Sajid Khan and Nauman Ali bowling in tandem and created pressure from both ends and Sajid Khan eventually took his first five-wicket haul to restrict Bangladesh to 76/7 at the end of Day 4. Sajid Khan took the wicket of Taijul Islam in his very first over on Day 5 and then Shaheen Afridi got rid of Khaled Ahmed in the very next over. Sajid Khan took the final wicket of Shakib Al Hasan and finished with eight wickets in the end. Pakistan have enforced the follow-on with a lead of 213 runs. They are in with a real chance now and Pakistan will be hoping that they can continue their good work from the first innings.

Bangladesh's innings started on the worst possible note as Mahmudul Hasan Joy, the debutant departed for a duck in his first innings. Soon his opening partner followed him and wickets continued to crumble as none of the batters showed the application to spend some time in the middle. They came out with bizarre tactics of going for their shots on every possible opportunity and paid the price in return. Shakib Al Hasan their star all-rounder was their only hope on Day 5 morning but wickets kept falling at the other end and Bangladesh have been bundled out for 87 and Pakistan have enforced the follow-on!

OUT! TAKEN! Sajid Khan takes the last wicket and he finishes with eight wickets to his name! Flatter ball, around off. Shakib Al Hasan skips down to go over extra cover but he fails to get the elevation and hits it straight to Azhar Ali at cover who takes a sharp catch. Bangladesh are bundled out for 87 and Pakistan have imposed the follow-on.
Commentary.Howout: c Azhar Ali b Sajid Khan

This match needed some very dreadful cricket from one team to take us to a result and Bangladesh have done exactly that on Day 4. It is now upto Pakistan to build on that and get early wickets on Day 5 to put Bangladesh under more pressure on this final day. Pakistan seamers were not allowed to bowl yesterday after the first over because of fading light, but they will be ready to explode this morning and that makes the task of playing out this day even tougher for Bangladesh. The pitch is difficult to bat on and the quality of Pakistan bowlers makes it more daunting for Bangladesh. From Bangladesh point of view, they need to show some application out there in the middle. They came out with bizarre tactics of going for their shots despite wickets falling at regular intervals and if they bat in the same way on Day 5, then only rain can help them in this Test match. Talking about the weather, it looks promising compared to the previous four days of this Test match and that makes up for a thrilling final day of Test cricket. Stay tuned.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 5 of the second Test between Bangladesh and Pakistan. After two days of almost no cricket, the action on Day 4 finally provided cricket fans with some exciting cricket. The first session was delayed due to the wet outfield, but once the game started it was Pakistan who dominated the proceedings and have now taken the game to a situation where they are in with a real chance of victory on Day 5. Day 4 started with Bangladesh seamers bowling in good areas and getting rid of overnight Pakistan batters very early in the day. But things went downhill after that as first Fawad Alam and Mohammad Rizwan stitched together a century stand as Pakistan declared for 300. Then, Pakistan spinners and especially Sajid Khan who bagged six wickets completely dismantled Bangladesh batting as they are left tottering at 76/7 after the end of day 4 with 25 more needed to avoid follow on. Can Bangla Tigers salvage a draw in this Test match? Or will Pakistan hand Bangladesh a humiliating defeat in their own backyard? An interesting day of Test cricket coming up.
... Day 5, Session 1 …

Right then! This brings us to an end of an exciting Day 4 of this Test match after we were greeted by only rain in the previous two days. The forecast for Day 5 looks promising and we can expect another cracking day of Test cricket from these two teams. Do join us at 9:30 am local time (3:30 am GMT). Till then, goodbye and cheers!

Earlier in the day, after a late start to the first session, Bangladesh bowlers struck early to send back both the overnight batters back to the pavilion. But another brilliant century stand between Fawad Alam and Mohammad Rizwan took Pakistan to 300 before they eventually declared. The bowlers came in with some aggressive attitude and picked three Bangladesh wickets for almost nothing and that set the tone for a brilliant post-Tea session.

Bangladesh batters came out like they were chasing 201 in 20 overs here. They tried to hit every ball that was possible for them and ended up losing wickets at regular intervals. Mushfiqur Rahim was first to go early in the session but the shot-making continued even though wickets were falling regularly. It took bad light to stop them from self-exploding and in the end, they have lost a total of seven wickets and it looks too tough for Bangladesh from hereon.

Another session that was pocketed by Pakistan. The spin bowlers bowling in tandem were brilliant and kept the pressure on as Bangladesh batters came out with bizarre tactics. Sajid Khan got rid of Mushfiqur Rahim early in the session and got another wicket of Liton Das as Bangladesh batters looked in some sort of a strange hurry. The off-spinner then went onto take six wickets as Bangladesh batters struggled to show any application in the middle. Pakistan have taken seven wickets in no time and despite the rain and bad light, they are in with a chance to win this Test match.

Drinks! What a bizarre piece of batting by Bangladesh here! Okay, scratch that. The umpires have decided to end the day's play as the light is not enough. Pakistan would be mighty pleased with their show on Day 4 and a result looks likely now!

Bangladesh batters were helped by the fact that seamers were not allowed to bowl after the first over but that advantage did not last long. Mahmudul Hasan Joy on debut was unable to get off the mark in Test cricket as he went for a duck. Shanto joined Shadman Islam and both played out some overs after that. But just when one thought that they will not lose any further wicket, Shadman Islam departed in the ninth over, and just at the stroke of Tea, the Bangldeah skipper Mominul Haque was run out to sink them further. Can Bangladesh batters display better technique and skills in the next session? We shall find out. Join us for the same at 3:30 pm local (9:30 am GMT).

Some good aggressive intent shown by Pakistan in this short passage of play before Tea. The innings started with Shaheen Afridi setting the tone with a brilliant first over. But then the umpires decided that only spin can be bowled and both the spinners kept the pressure on as they bowled good nagging lines and lengths. They were getting some sharp turn and Sajid Khan got rid of debutant Mahmudul Hasan Joy for a duck. Khan went onto get another big wicket towards the fag end of the session. In the end, a good piece of fielding from Hasan Ali also sent back Bangladesh skipper, Mominul Haque, to take Pakistan right on the top.

What a session for Pakistan! They got a pretty big score and have picked up 3 quick wickets! They are surely on top currently but they would hope that light doesn't play spoilsport in the last session.

Hasan Ali charges to the ball and fires a direct hit at the bowler's end. The TV umpire is called in and Mominul Haque is miles short of the crease! That also brings Tea on Day 4!
They have gone upstairs for a run out appeal. Mominul Haque is short of his crease as Hasan Ali fires in a good throw at the bowler's end. The third Bangladesh wicket goes down.
